q: Arjun's chatbot forgets the user's name from two messages earlier. What is the most likely reason?
options: The model's context window is too small for two messages
The temperature setting is too high for memory tasks
His code is not resending the conversation history, since the API is stateless
The system prompt is overriding the user's earlier messages
explain: The model has no memory between calls; your code must store the history and send it with every request.

q: A response comes back with stop_reason set to "max_tokens". What does this tell you?
options: The answer was cut off at the output limit, so raise the limit or ask for a shorter answer
The model finished normally and the answer is complete
The model wants to call a tool before answering
The model declined the request for safety reasons
explain: max_tokens means the output hit the ceiling and is truncated; log it and adjust rather than showing a half answer.

q: Why does the course loop over response.content and check each block's type instead of using response.content[0].text?
options: Looping is faster than indexing for large responses
The first block is always the system prompt, not the answer
Indexing does not work with streaming responses
Responses can contain tool_use or thinking blocks, so the first block may not be text
explain: Code that assumes the first block is text works in demos but breaks once tools or other block types appear.

q: An extraction schema has a required budget field, and the model fills in a number when the enquiry never mentions one. What is the best fix?
options: Ask the model to return free-text JSON and parse it with regex
Make the field nullable and instruct the model to use null and not guess
Remove the budget field and estimate it later in code
Add a second model call to double-check every number
explain: Nullable fields plus a "do not guess" instruction are the main defence against invented values.

q: In the GST invoice project, how does the service check that CGST, SGST and the totals add up?
options: It asks the model a second time whether the totals look right
Deterministic Python checks verify the model's extracted values
It trusts the schema, since constrained output guarantees correct values
It sends the invoice to a second model and compares answers
explain: The model reads and structures; deterministic code verifies, since a schema guarantees shape, not truth.

q: A customer asks about two orders and the model returns two tool_use blocks. How should your code respond?
options: Run only the first tool and ignore the second request
Send each tool result in a separate user message, one after another
Combine both results into plain text without any IDs
Run both and return all tool_result blocks, each with its tool_use_id, in one user message
explain: Every tool_result must carry the matching tool_use_id, and all results go back together in a single message.

q: Meena embeds her documents with one model and user queries with a different embedding model. What will happen?
options: Search results will be unreliable, because vectors from different models are not comparable
Search will be faster because each model is specialised
Results will be identical as long as both vectors are normalised
Chroma will automatically convert the vectors to the same space
explain: You must use the same embedding model for documents and queries, since vectors from different models do not share a space.

q: Users search a RAG app for an exact invoice number like "INV-2026-0417" and get a different invoice. What does the course suggest?
options: Increase the embedding model's vector dimension
Remove all numbers from documents before embedding
Use hybrid search that combines keyword search with vector search
Lower the temperature of the answering model
explain: Embeddings are weak at exact codes and names, so hybrid keyword plus vector search is common in production.

q: Your RAG app retrieved 5 chunks, but the model cites source 7. What should the rendering code do?
options: Check every source ID is within range before using it to index the chunk list
Show source 7 anyway, since the model knows best
Re-run retrieval with k=7 so the citation becomes valid
Crash the request so the error is noticed
explain: Never trust model output to index into your lists; validate each source ID before rendering citations.

q: You want to evaluate your invoice extractor on fields like GSTIN and invoice number. Which check does the course recommend?
options: An LLM judge grading each invoice on a 1-10 scale
Reading a few outputs manually and noting whether they look fine
Exact or tolerance comparison against expected values in code
Asking the extraction model to rate its own confidence
explain: When the right answer is exact, deterministic code checks are cheaper and more trustworthy than LLM judges.

q: Why must every agent loop include a max_steps limit?
options: The API rejects requests that contain more than a few tools
It makes the model choose better tools on the first try
It reduces the size of each tool's output
A confused agent could otherwise loop many times and burn budget
explain: max_steps is the circuit breaker that stops runaway loops; every shipped agent needs one.

q: In the CSV analyst agent, why does the calculator parse expressions with ast instead of using Python's eval()?
options: ast is faster than eval() for large numbers
eval() would execute any code the model writes, which is unsafe
eval() cannot handle division or percentages
ast automatically formats results in Indian rupees
explain: The safe calculator evaluates only numbers and basic operators; eval() on model output could run arbitrary code.

q: A task always runs the same steps in order: extract fields, validate them, save to a database. What should you build?
options: A multi-step agent with tools for each step
An agent with a planning step and human checkpoint
An agent with a higher step limit for reliability
A fixed workflow in code, since the steps are known in advance
explain: When steps are known in advance, a fixed workflow is cheaper, faster and easier to test than an agent.

q: After adding the current date and time to the start of his system prompt, Rohit sees cache_read_input_tokens drop to zero. Why?
options: Caching is an exact prefix match, and the changing timestamp breaks it
Dates are not allowed inside cached content
The cache only works for prompts without any numbers
Caching is disabled whenever the system prompt changes length
explain: One changed character early in the prefix invalidates the cache; put volatile info after the cached part.

q: Which API error should your app generally NOT retry automatically?
options: A 429 rate-limit error
A 400-type error such as a bad request or invalid key
A temporary 5xx server error
A network connection timeout
explain: Retry rate limits, server and network errors with backoff; 400-type errors need the cause fixed, not retries.

q: Your FastAPI app works locally but is unreachable inside its Docker container. What is a classic cause?
options: The Dockerfile copies the code before installing requirements
The container runs as a non-root user
The server binds to 127.0.0.1 instead of 0.0.0.0
The .env file was listed in .dockerignore
explain: Binding to 127.0.0.1 makes the server unreachable from outside the container; use --host 0.0.0.0.

q: What makes the Results section of a portfolio README most persuasive to interviewers?
options: Real numbers from your own evaluation set, such as 17/20 correct
A general claim that the app is highly accurate
A long list of every AI framework you have heard of
Screenshots of the code without any measurements
explain: Honest, specific evaluation numbers beat vague claims; never invent them.

q: An interviewer asks: for an HR policy bot whose policies change every quarter, would you use RAG or fine-tuning?
options: Fine-tuning, because it teaches the model facts permanently
Fine-tuning, because it avoids sending documents with each query
RAG, because updating means re-ingesting documents, not retraining
Neither; put all policies in the system prompt with no retrieval
explain: RAG brings in fresh or private knowledge at query time, so changing policies only need re-ingestion.
